sentence_stem: Had the manuscript not been lost in the flood,
correct_completion: the author would have published her most celebrated novel a decade earlier.
full_sentence: Had the manuscript not been lost in the flood, the author would have published her most celebrated novel a decade earlier.
acceptable_variants: the novel would have appeared a decade earlier.
the author would certainly have published it sooner.

options.text: so the author never finished the novel.
options.why_wrong: 'So' introduces a result of the loss, but the stem requires a hypothetical past consequence introduced by an inverted third conditional.

options.text: the author would have published her most celebrated novel a decade earlier.
the author publishes the novel every year.
options.why_wrong: The present simple describes a habit and contradicts the unreal past situation set up by 'had ... not been'.

options.text: the author will have finished the novel by now.
options.why_wrong: A future perfect form does not complete an unreal past condition; the stem requires 'would have' followed by a past participle.

grammar_focus: Inverted third conditional with 'had' and past perfect passive
explanation: The inverted form 'Had ... not been' replaces 'If ... had not been' and sets up an unreal past condition. The main clause must use 'would have' plus a past participle to express the imagined result. Ukrainian speakers may find this hard because Ukrainian expresses hypothetical meaning with a past-tense form plus a particle, not with a separate perfect auxiliary.
translation: Якби рукопис не загубився під час повені, авторка опублікувала б свій найвідоміший роман на десять років раніше.
